mainTopic: What the word הַכֹּל adds: moving to ארץ ישראל and ירושלים, and why כהנים are obligated in סוכה, ציצית, תפילין and שופר
overview: The גמרא goes through several teachings that begin with the word הַכֹּל ('everyone') and asks what each one adds. It first finishes the משנה about moving to ארץ ישראל and ירושלים. 'Everyone' includes slaves, a move from a nice home to a poor one, a runaway slave who reached ארץ ישראל, and the rule that a family may not be forced out of ירושלים even to a better home. Then it brings a series of ברייתות saying that כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are all obligated in סוכה, ציצית, תפילין and שופר. Each time the גמרא asks 'isn't that obvious?' and explains why we might have exempted כהנים: they are busy with the עבודה, they may wear כלאים, they cannot wear hand תפילין, or they blow all year. Each mistaken idea is rejected: the exemption covers only the time of the עבודה, or hand and head תפילין are separate מצוות. For שופר, the first reason is pushed off because trumpets are not a שופר. A new reason, linking ראש השנה to יובל, begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The word 'everyone' comes to include slaves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers what הַכֹּל מַעֲלִין לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל comes to include: slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question it just asked: what does 'everyone can force others to move up to ארץ ישראל' come to add? It says the word 'everyone' includes slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the word הַכֹּל, we might think only free family members can push for a move to ארץ ישראל. The word 'everyone' teaches that even an עבד can make his master either move with him, sell him to someone who will, or free him.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, to bring in an extra case
Make others move up (to ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: To include slaves,

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוֹיֵי עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier question about what הַכֹּל מַעֲלִין לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל includes
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word הַכֹּל includes slaves, who can also force a move to ארץ ישראל

steps.title: What if slaves are already listed openly?
steps.stepSummary: According to the version of the משנה that lists slaves outright, the word 'everyone' can't be there to include them, so what does it add?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who teaches slaves explicitly in the משנה, what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. Some versions of the משנה already mention slaves directly, so the word 'everyone' must be adding something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If slaves are written right there in the משנה, then 'everyone' is not needed for them. The גמרא assumes every word in the משנה teaches something, so it looks for a different case. This step sets up the next answer.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who teaches (a certain version)

phrases.english: And according to the one who teaches slaves explicitly,
phrases.notes: Some versions of this משנה openly list slaves among the people who can force a move.

phrases.english: what does it come to include?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּתָנֵי עֲבָדִים בְּהֶדְיָא, לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that the answer in step 1 does not work for the version that already mentions slaves
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What הַכֹּל adds for the version of the משנה that already lists slaves

steps.title: Even from a nice home to a poor one
steps.stepSummary: The word 'everyone' includes forcing a move to ארץ ישראל even when it means leaving a nice home for a poor one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include moving from a pleasant home to a poor home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: 'everyone' teaches that a person can force his family to move to ארץ ישראל even if they would go from a beautiful home outside the land to a poor home inside it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here הַכֹּל is read as 'in every situation' rather than 'every kind of person.' Even when the move makes their living conditions worse, living in ארץ ישראל wins, and the family can be made to go.

phrases.english: To include moving from a pleasant home to a poor home.
phrases.notes: He means from a nice home outside ארץ ישראל to a poorer one inside it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוֹיֵי מִנָּוֶה הַיָּפָה לְנָוֶה הָרָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הַכֹּל includes a move to ארץ ישראל even from a nice home to a worse one
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much weight הלכה gives to living in ארץ ישראל: it beats comfort.

steps.title: A runaway slave cannot be taken out of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The second half, 'not everyone can take others out,' includes a slave who ran from outside the land into ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not everyone can take out' comes to include a slave who fled from outside the land into the land.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second half of the same משנה. 'Not everyone can take others out' teaches that a master can't bring back a slave who ran away into ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a master has rights over his runaway slave. But once the slave has reached ארץ ישראל, the master cannot drag him back outside, because leaving the land is treated so seriously.

phrases.english: 'And not everyone can take out' —
comes to include a slave who fled
from outside the land to the land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין הַכֹּל מוֹצִיאִין — לְאֵתוֹיֵי עֶבֶד שֶׁבָּרַח מֵחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first half of the משנה to its second half
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave who ran into ארץ ישראל may not be taken back out by his master

steps.title: Moving up to ירושלים, even to a worse home
steps.stepSummary: 'Everyone can bring up to ירושלים' includes a move from a nice home outside ירושלים to a poor one inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Everyone can bring up to ירושלים' comes to include moving from a pleasant home to a poor home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the same משנה, about ירושלים. It says 'everyone' teaches that a family can be made to move to ירושלים even if their new home there is worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the rule for ארץ ישראל in step 3, one level up. ירושלים holds a higher holiness, so moving there is worth losing comfort.

phrases.english: 'Everyone can bring up to Jerusalem' —
comes to include from a pleasant home to a poor home,

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל מַעֲלִין לִירוּשָׁלַיִם — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מִנָּוֶה הַיָּפָה לְנָוֶה הָרָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'nice home to poor home' idea to ירושלים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may force a move to ירושלים even from a nice home to a worse one

steps.title: What does 'not taking out of ירושלים' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the second half of the ירושלים line comes to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not everyone can take out': what does it come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what 'not everyone can take out of ירושלים' adds. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'nice home to poor home' case has already been used for moving into ירושלים, and the slave case was used for ארץ ישראל. So the גמרא needs a new case for this half.

phrases.english: 'And not everyone can take out' —
phrases.notes: This time it means taking someone out of ירושלים.

phrases.english: what does it come to include?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין הַכֹּל מוֹצִיאִין — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the second half of the ירושלים line from step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra case 'not everyone can take out of ירושלים' teaches

steps.title: Not even from a poor home to a nice one
steps.stepSummary: You can't force a family out of ירושלים, even to leave a poor home there for a nice home elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include even from a poor home to a pleasant home.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: you may not force your family to leave ירושלים, even when they'd be moving from a poor home to a much nicer one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the mirror image of step 5. Moving in is allowed even when it makes things worse, and moving out is blocked even when it would make things better.
steps.whatToRemember: For both ארץ ישראל and ירושלים, you may force a family to move in, even from a nice home to a worse one. For ירושלים, you may not force them out, even to a better home. For ארץ ישראל, 'not everyone can take out' adds a runaway slave who reached the land. Each word הַכֹּל adds a new case.

phrases.english: To include from a poor home to a pleasant home.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאֵתוֹיֵי מִנָּוֶה הָרָעָה לְנָוֶה הַיָּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One may not force a family out of ירושלים even from a poor home to a nice one

steps.title: Everyone is obligated in סוכה
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: everyone, כהנים, לוים and ישראלים, must sit in a סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone is obligated in סוכה: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching that also starts with הַכֹּל: everyone must keep the מצוה of סוכה, and it lists כהנים, לוים and ישראלים. This sets up a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic in the same pattern of 'everyone' teachings. The list of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים seems to just name the regular Jewish people, which is why the next step will ask why it needs saying.

keyTerms.meaning: The booth Jews live in during סוכות
Priests, Levites and regular Jews: the three groups of the Jewish people

phrases.english: Everyone is obligated in sukka,
priests, Levites, and Israelites.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בְּסוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new 'הַכֹּל' teaching after finishing the ארץ ישראל and ירושלים one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are all obligated in סוכה

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if כהנים, לוים and ישראלים weren't obligated, who would be? So why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! If these aren't obligated, who is obligated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are simply all of the Jewish people, so of course they're obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא expects every teaching to tell us something new. Listing the most basic groups seems to add nothing, so the ברייתא must have some hidden point. The answer will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (a challenge that a teaching adds nothing)

phrases.english: That is obvious!
If these are not obligated,
who is obligated?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא! אִי הָנֵי לָא מִחַיְּיבִי, מַאן מִיחַיְּיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's list of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These groups make up all Jews, so saying they are obligated seems to teach nothing new

steps.title: Why we might have exempted כהנים from סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא needed to mention כהנים. Since a סוכה must be lived in like a home (a man with his wife), we might have thought that busy כהנים are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא needed to mention כהנים. You might have thought this: the פסוק says 'in סוכות you shall dwell', and the Master taught that dwelling in the סוכה must be like living in a home. A home is a man and his wife living together, so a סוכה should also be a man and his wife. כהנים are busy with the Temple service, so maybe they are not obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question 'why say it?' It explains that the ברייתא mentioned כהנים because we might have wrongly exempted them. This step only sets up the mistaken idea; the real lesson comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that a סוכה must be like a regular home (תדורו) means a person lives there the normal way, with his wife. כהנים are busy with the עבודה during the חג and can't live in the סוכה that way. So it might seem the whole מצוה doesn't apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed (he needed to say it)
You might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
Like the way you normally live at home
A home, the normal way of living
People busy with the Temple service

steps.confusionAlert: This step is NOT the conclusion. It is only the mistaken idea (סלקא דעתך) that the ברייתא comes to reject.

phrases.english: It was needed for him to mention priests,
since it could enter your mind to say:
since it is written: 'In sukkot you shall dwell,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר מָר ״תֵּשְׁבוּ שִׁבְעַת יָמִים״ כְּעֵין תָּדוּרוּ,
phrases.english: and the Master said: 'Dwell seven days' means like the way you live at home,
just as a home is a man and his wife,
so too a sukka is a man and his wife,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי כֹּהֲנִים הוֹאִיל וּבְנֵי עֲבוֹדָה נִינְהוּ —
phrases.english: and these priests, since they are busy with the service,
should not be obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֲנִים אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the 'why say it?' question of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the mention is not obvious by presenting a reasonable mistaken idea (הוה אמינא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a סוכה must be lived in like a home with one's wife, כהנים who are busy with עבודה would be exempt.

steps.title: כהנים are exempt only while serving, like travelers
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that כהנים are exempt only during the עבודה and obligated at other times, just like travelers are exempt by day and obligated at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the ברייתא teaches us: even though they are exempt while doing the service, when they are not serving they are obligated. It is just like travelers, as the Master said: people traveling by day are exempt from סוכה during the day but obligated at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real lesson of the ברייתא: כהנים are obligated in סוכה whenever they are not busy serving. It proves this with the case of travelers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being busy at certain times does not cancel the whole מצוה. It only exempts you during those busy hours. Travelers show this clearly: they are exempt only while on the road, and they still must use a סוכה at night.

keyTerms.meaning: Just like the case of (a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: An exemption tied to a specific activity lasts only while you are doing it. כהנים are exempt from סוכה only during the עבודה, just as travelers are exempt only while traveling.

phrases.english: It teaches us:
granted that they are exempt at the time of the service,
when it is not the time of the service they are certainly obligated,
just like the case of travelers,
as the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹלְכֵי דְרָכִים בַּיּוֹם פְּטוּרִין מִן הַסּוּכָּה בַּיּוֹם,
phrases.english: those who travel by day are exempt from the sukka during the day,
and are obligated at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: נְהִי דִּפְטִירִי בִּשְׁעַת עֲבוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the mistaken idea of step 10 and gives the real lesson
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the exemption to the time of service, supported by a parallel case
steps.terutzMaskana: כהנים are exempt from סוכה only during the עבודה and obligated otherwise, like travelers who are exempt by day but obligated at night.

steps.title: Everyone, including כהנים, must wear ציצית
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: everyone is obligated in ציצית, כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone is obligated in ציצית: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא with the same wording as the סוכה one, this time about ציצית. It is setting up the same 'why say it?' question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the exact pattern of step 8. Again the ברייתא lists all three groups, which seems unnecessary.

phrases.english: Everyone is obligated in ritual fringes,
priests, Levites, and Israelites.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בְּצִיצִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new parallel ברייתא, same pattern as step 8
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are all obligated in ציצית.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to say this, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ציצית ברייתא, just as it challenged the סוכה ברייתא: who else would be obligated if not these three groups?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on wording. If כהנים, לוים and ישראלים make up all of the Jewish people, listing them adds nothing. So there must be a hidden reason for the list.

phrases.english: That's obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The listing of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים in the ציצית ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everyone obviously includes these three groups, so stating it seems pointless.

steps.title: Why we might have exempted כהנים from ציצית
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא needed to mention כהנים. The פסוק puts ציצית right next to the ban on שעטנז, so we might think only people forbidden in כלאים need ציצית, and כהנים are allowed כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא needed to mention כהנים. You might have thought this: the Torah writes 'Do not wear שעטנז...' and right after it 'Make yourself fringes.' So only someone who is not allowed to wear כלאים is obligated in ציצית. Since כהנים are allowed to wear כלאים, they should not be obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer in the same way as for סוכה: it shows why we might have exempted כהנים from ציצית. This step only presents the mistaken idea that the ברייתא comes to reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two פסוקים sit side by side, which suggests a link: ציצית is for people who are bound by the כלאים ban. כהנים are allowed to wear כלאים in their service clothing, so the link seems to exempt them. The ברייתא tells us that this idea is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden mix of wool and linen in clothing

steps.confusionAlert: This is the mistaken idea (סלקא דעתך), not the הלכה. The ברייתא's point is that כהנים ARE obligated in ציצית.

phrases.english: It was needed for him to mention priests,
since it could enter your mind to say:
since it is written: 'You shall not wear shaatnez...'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:11–12. The link comes from these two פסוקים sitting right next to each other.

phrases.english: 'You shall make yourself twisted cords,'

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּלָא אִישְׁתְּרִי כִּלְאַיִם לְגַבֵּיהּ בִּלְבִישָׁה
phrases.english: one for whom diverse kinds are not permitted to wear
is the one who is obligated in the מצוה of fringes,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָנֵי כֹּהֲנִים, הוֹאִיל וְאִישְׁתְּרִי כִּלְאַיִם לְגַבַּיְיהוּ,
phrases.english: and these priests, since diverse kinds were permitted for them,
should not be obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֲנִים אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the 'obvious' challenge of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the mention is not obvious by presenting a reasonable mistaken idea (הוה אמינא) drawn from the closeness of the פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since ציצית is written next to the שעטנז ban, only those forbidden in כלאים need ציצית, and כהנים, who are permitted כלאים, would be exempt.

steps.title: כהנים are permitted כלאים only during the עבודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that כהנים may wear כלאים only during the עבודה, not at other times, so they are obligated in ציצית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא teaches us: even though כהנים are allowed to wear כלאים during the עבודה, they are not allowed when it is not the time of the עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from step 14. It explains why the ברייתא had to tell us that כהנים must wear ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 we thought only people who are forbidden in כלאים need ציצית, and כהנים are allowed כלאים. The answer is that their permission covers only the time of the עבודה. The rest of the time they are forbidden in כלאים like everyone else, so they are obligated in ציצית.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (the new point the source is making)
The time of the Temple service

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן's permission to wear כלאים is limited to the time of the עבודה. Outside that time he is like everyone else and must wear ציצית.

phrases.english: It teaches us:
even though they are permitted at the time of the service,
when it is not the time of the service, they are not permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 14 by stating what the ברייתא actually teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of an exemption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כהנים are allowed כלאים, so they are not obligated in ציצית.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their permission is only during the עבודה, so they are obligated in ציצית.

steps.title: Everyone is obligated in תפילין
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are all obligated in תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone is obligated in תפילין: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא, built just like the ones about סוכה and ציצית. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the third ברייתא in the same pattern. Once again it lists כהנים, לוים and ישראלים. The גמרא will ask why this needed to be said.

keyTerms.meaning: תפילין, the boxes with פסוקים worn on the arm and head

phrases.english: Everyone is obligated in tefillin,
priests, Levites, and Israelites.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בִּתְפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא following the same pattern as the סוכה and ציצית ברייתות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are all obligated in תפילין.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to say that everyone is obligated in תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא bothers to say something that seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are all Jewish men, and there is no clear reason any of them would be exempt. So listing them seems pointless. The question pushes us to find the hidden point.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. Why say it?

phrases.english: Isn't that obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling seems obvious, so a ברייתא should not need to teach it.

steps.title: The פסוק links hand and head תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא needed to mention כהנים. The פסוק puts hand and head תפילין together, so we might think only someone obligated in hand תפילין is obligated in head תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for כהנים. You might have thought: since the פסוק says "bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be frontlets between your eyes," anyone obligated in hand תפילין is obligated in head תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by laying out the first half of the mistaken idea. It is setting up why כהנים might seem exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hand תפילין and head תפילין appear together in one פסוק. From that we might think they go together: the head obligation depends on the hand obligation. The next step will explain why that matters for כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought to say

phrases.english: It was necessary for priests,
since it might enter your mind to say:
since it is written
"And you shall bind them for a sign upon your hand,
and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes,"
anyone who is included in the מצוה of the arm
is included in the מצוה of the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֲנִים אִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the פשיטא question with a הוה אמינא built on the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a reasonable mistaken idea (הוה אמינא) that the ברייתא rules out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the פסוק joins hand and head, the head obligation depends on the hand obligation.
steps.terutzMaskana: Completed in step 20: they do not depend on each other.

steps.title: כהנים cannot wear hand תפילין during the עבודה
steps.stepSummary: כהנים are not obligated in hand תפילין during the עבודה, because nothing may come between their בגדי כהונה and their skin. So we might think they are not obligated in head תפילין either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these כהנים are not included in the מצוה of hand תפילין, because it is written "he shall wear upon his flesh," meaning nothing may separate between him and his flesh. So you might say they are not obligated in head תפילין either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the mistaken idea. It applies the hand-head link from step 18 to כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בגדי כהונה must touch the כהן's skin directly. Arm תפילין would be in the way, so a כהן during the עבודה cannot wear them. If head depends on hand, the כהן would be exempt from head תפילין too.

keyTerms.meaning: Separates or blocks; something in between
He shall wear upon his flesh (the בגדי כהונה must touch the skin)

steps.confusionAlert: The כהן is not exempt from hand תפילין because he is a כהן. It is only during the עבודה, when the בגדי כהונה must touch his skin, that hand תפילין would get in the way.

phrases.english: And these priests,
since they are not included in the מצוה of the arm,
as it is written: "He shall put upon his flesh,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:3, said about the בגדי כהונה.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא דָּבָר חוֹצֵץ בֵּינוֹ וּבֵין בְּשָׂרוֹ,
phrases.english: so that nothing should separate between it and his flesh,
phrases.notes: "It" means the priestly garment. The arm תפילין would sit between the sleeve and the skin.

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא בְּמִצְוָה דְרֹאשׁ נָמֵי לָא לִיחַיְּיבוּ.
phrases.english: say that they should also not be obligated in the מצוה of the head.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי כֹּהֲנִים, הוֹאִיל וְלֵיתַנְהוּ בְּמִצְוָה דְיָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the hand-head link from step 18 to כהנים to complete the mistaken idea.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כהנים cannot wear hand תפילין during the עבודה, so they would be exempt from head תפילין too.

steps.title: Hand and head תפילין do not depend on each other
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that hand and head תפילין do not hold each other back, as a משנה states. So כהנים are obligated in head תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא teaches us that they do not hold each other back, as we learned in a משנה: hand תפילין do not hold back head תפילין, and head תפילין do not hold back hand תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the conclusion: the ברייתא teaches that hand and head תפילין are separate מצוות. It supports this with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistaken idea assumed that head תפילין depend on hand תפילין. The משנה says each one is a separate מצוה, and lacking one does not stop you from doing the other. So a כהן who cannot wear hand תפילין during the עבודה still must wear head תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back, so the מצוה cannot be done without it

steps.whatToRemember: Hand and head תפילין are two separate מצוות. Missing one does not cancel the other, so כהנים during the עבודה still wear head תפילין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical rule in הלכה: if someone has only one of the תפילין, he still puts on the one he has.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא מְעַכְּבִי אַהֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: It teaches us that they do not hold each other back,
as we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִלָּה שֶׁל יָד אֵינָהּ מְעַכֶּבֶת שֶׁל רֹאשׁ,
phrases.english: the tefillin of the arm does not hold back that of the head,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁל רֹאשׁ אֵינָהּ מְעַכֶּבֶת שֶׁל יָד.
phrases.english: and that of the head does not hold back that of the arm.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא מְעַכְּבִי אַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the mistaken idea from steps 18-19 and states what the ברייתא teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the הוה אמינא with a משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Head תפילין depend on hand תפילין, so כהנים are exempt from both.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two do not depend on each other, so כהנים are obligated in head תפילין.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא lists כהנים to teach that hand and head תפילין are separate מצוות, so כהנים must wear head תפילין even during the עבודה.

steps.title: Why is the head different from the hand?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that כהנים are obligated in head תפילין. The head should be blocked by the מצנפת, just as the arm is blocked by the בגדי כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the hand תפילין? Because it is written 'he shall put on upon his flesh'? For the head it is also written 'and you shall put the turban on his head'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the answer from the last step. If the arm is exempt because the clothing must touch the skin, the head should be exempt too, because the מצנפת must sit on the head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 said that nothing may come between the בגדי כהונה and the כהן's body, so hand תפילין are not worn during the עבודה. The גמרא points out that the same idea seems to apply to the head, since the פסוק says the מצנפת goes 'on his head'. If so, why did step 20 say כהנים are obligated in head תפילין?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asks why two cases are treated differently)
Upon his flesh: the clothing must touch the body directly
The turban of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: And what is different about the hand [תפילין],
that it is written: 'he shall put on upon his flesh'?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:3, the same source from step 19.

phrases.english: The head also,
it is written: 'And you shall put the turban on his head'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא דְּיָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction between hand and head that steps 19 and 20 depend on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that כהנים are obligated in head תפילין even though they are exempt from hand תפילין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason that exempts the hand (the clothing must touch the body) seems to apply to the head too, because the מצנפת must sit 'on his head'.

steps.title: There was room for תפילין between the ציץ and the מצנפת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the כהן גדול's hair showed between the ציץ and the מצנפת. That is where he put his head תפילין, so they did not block anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: His hair was visible between the ציץ and the מצנפת, and there he would put on תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. There was an open space on the head where the תפילין could go without getting in the way of the clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ sat low on the forehead and the מצנפת sat higher up, so some hair showed in between. The head תפילין went in that gap. Nothing came between the מצנפת and the head, so the problem from the arm does not apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: The gold plate worn on the כהן גדול's forehead

steps.whatToRemember: The hand is different from the head. On the arm, תפילין would block the clothing. On the head there was a free gap between the ציץ and the מצנפת, so כהנים can wear head תפילין.

phrases.english: It was taught: His hair was visible
between the frontplate and the turban,
for there he would put on תפילין.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: שְׂעָרוֹ הָיָה נִרְאֶה בֵּין צִיץ לְמִצְנֶפֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual distinction: the head had a free space, so the two cases are not the same
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Head תפילין would block the מצנפת just as hand תפילין would block the clothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Head תפילין sat in the gap between the ציץ and the מצנפת, so they blocked nothing.

steps.title: Everyone is obligated in שופר
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are all obligated in תקיעת שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone is obligated in blowing the שופר: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that starts with 'everyone', like the ones before it. This one is about blowing the שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא has the same pattern as the תפילין one in step 16. It lists all three groups as obligated. The גמרא will now ask why it needed to say this.

keyTerms.meaning: Blowing the שופר on ראש השנה

phrases.english: Everyone is obligated in blowing the shofar,
priests, Levites and Israelites.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין בִּתְקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about שופר, following the same 'everyone' pattern as the תפילין ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לוים and ישראלים are all obligated in תקיעת שופר.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needs to say this. It seems obvious that everyone must hear the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא bothered to list everyone. Of course all Jews are obligated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא should not waste words on something obvious. So the גמרא expects there must be a hidden reason one of the groups needed to be mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (asks why something needed to be said)

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the ברייתא in step 23 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the ברייתא, which lists all three groups.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no reason to think any group of Jews is exempt, so listing them seems pointless.

steps.title: The ברייתא needed to mention כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא needed to mention כהנים. Since the פסוק calls ראש השנה a 'day of blowing', we might think it applies only to someone who blows on just that one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It needed to mention כהנים. You might have thought: since it is written 'it shall be a day of blowing for you', only someone who blows on just one day is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer: the new point is about כהנים. Here it sets up the first half of the mistaken thought, and the next step will finish it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of one special 'day of blowing'. From that we might think the מצוה is only for people whose blowing happens on that one day of the year. This is the first part of the הוה אמינא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him (the ברייתא needed to say it)

phrases.english: It was necessary for him [to mention] priests,
it could enter your mind to say:
since it is written: 'It shall be a day of blowing for you,'
one who is not [obligated] except
in blowing on one day, is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֲנִים אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the פשיטא of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: the ברייתא is needed to block a mistaken idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'day of blowing' obligation is only for people who blow on that one day alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: To be completed in the next step: the ברייתא teaches that כהנים are obligated too.

steps.title: כהנים blow all year, so we might think they are exempt
steps.stepSummary: כהנים blow in the מקדש all year over the קרבנות. So we might have said they are not obligated in שופר on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these כהנים, since they blow all year, as it is written 'and you shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings', say they should not be obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the mistaken thought. כהנים blow all year long, so ראש השנה is not a special 'one day' for them, and we might have exempted them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the מצוה might belong only to people who blow on one day. כהנים blow over the קרבנות all year, so they do not fit that description. That is why the ברייתא had to tell us that כהנים are obligated too.

keyTerms.meaning: Trumpets (blown by כהנים in the מקדש)

phrases.english: But these priests,
since they are [involved] in blowing the whole year,
as it is written: 'And you shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings,'
I might say they should not be obligated.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Could be seen as the second half of one long תירוץ together with step 25.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי כֹּהֲנִים, הוֹאִיל וְאִיתַנְהוּ בִּתְקִיעָה כּוּלַּיהּ שַׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the הוה אמינא started in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: explains why כהנים had to be mentioned
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כהנים blow all year, so the 'one day of blowing' obligation would not apply to them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that כהנים are obligated in שופר anyway.

steps.title: Trumpets are not a שופר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the comparison: the year-round blowing is with חצוצרות, but on ראש השנה it is a שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable? There it is trumpets; here it is a shofar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reasoning it just gave. The two kinds of blowing are not the same, so why would we ever have thought כהנים are exempt?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הוה אמינא assumed that blowing all year makes ראש השנה nothing special for כהנים. But all year they blow חצוצרות, which are a different instrument, while the ראש השנה מצוה is with a שופר. So the mistaken thought seems too weak to need a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here (sets two cases side by side)

steps.confusionAlert: חצוצרות (metal trumpets) and a שופר (an animal's horn) are two different instruments. The whole challenge depends on telling them apart.

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
There it is trumpets,
here it is a shofar!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם חֲצוֹצְרוֹת, הָכָא שׁוֹפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the הוה אמינא given in steps 25 and 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning that blowing all year could exempt כהנים from שופר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The year-round blowing is with a different instrument (חצוצרות), so it cannot be compared to the שופר of ראש השנה.

steps.title: New reason: ראש השנה is linked to יובל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reason the ברייתא had to mention כהנים. A משנה says יובל and ראש השנה are the same for שופר and ברכות. So we might think that whoever is outside the מצוה of יובל is also outside the מצוה of ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought this: since we learned that the יובל is the same as ראש השנה for the blowing and for the blessings, then whoever is part of the מצוה of יובל is part of the מצוה of ראש השנה. And whoever is not part of the מצוה of יובל is not part of the מצוה of ראש השנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a fresh answer to why the ברייתא had to say כהנים must hear שופר. It is setting up a mistaken idea that the ברייתא needed to block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old idea was that כהנים blow all year. That failed, because their year-round blowing is with חצוצרות. The new idea is based on a משנה that ties ראש השנה to יובל. If the two are tied, we might think that someone left out of one is left out of the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed; the text had to say it
It might enter your mind to say (the mistaken first idea)
The Jubilee year, every fiftieth year
The special blessings added to the עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: The יובל here means יום כיפור of the יובל year, when the שופר is blown. It is not the whole year.

phrases.english: It was needed; it might enter your mind to say

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וּתְנַן: שָׁוֶה הַיּוֹבֵל לְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה
phrases.english: since we learned: the Jubilee is the same as Rosh HaShana
phrases.notes: This משנה is in ראש השנה 26b, and it's talking about יום כיפור of the יובל year.

phrases.english: for the blowing and for the blessings
so whoever is included in the מצוה of the Jubilee
is included in the מצוה of Rosh HaShana
and whoever is not included in the מצוה of the Jubilee
is not included in the מצוה of Rosh HaShana

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 27 with a new reason the ברייתא needed to mention כהנים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New הוה אמינא that justifies the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since יובל and ראש השנה are equal for שופר, someone outside the מצוה of יובל would be outside ראש השנה too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא had to tell us that כהנים are obligated anyway. This conclusion comes on the next amud.

steps.title: כהנים are not fully part of the laws of יובל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the idea to כהנים. They are not fully included in the laws of יובל, as a משנה shows: כהנים and לוים may sell their fields at any time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these כהנים, since they are not included in the מצוה of יובל, as we learned: כהנים and לוים sell forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that כהנים are not fully part of the laws of יובל, using a משנה as proof. It is still building the mistaken idea, and the ending comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the laws of יובל limit how a person's field is sold and returned. כהנים and לוים have their own rules for selling and are not limited the same way. So they seem outside the laws of יובל, and by the last step's logic, outside ראש השנה too.

keyTerms.meaning: Levites, members of the tribe of לוי
They may sell at any time

phrases.english: And these priests
since they are not included in the מצוה of the Jubilee
as we learned: priests and Levites may sell at any time
phrases.notes: He means their fields. They are not held to the normal יובל rules for selling land.
